title: The project's history is controlled by review, not by a gate
situation: The record gate refused, in every commit and in CI, any change to an existing record, and so blocked the release of the operator's own documented green-field reset twice. It applied the product's rule, that the concept journal is append-only through the journal tool, to the development of cratylus, a different context. The operator, 2026-10-13: the record gate, the ledger's misreading and the CI's special checks are grey-field patches; the conceptual model conflated the bounded context of the product's users with the context of developing and releasing the product, which dogfoods the workflow but is a context of its own.
decision: In the development context the history changes by pull request and is controlled by its review; no hook, CI step or command refuses a change to the history. In the product, the journal is append-only because its tool offers only appending verbs, by construction, and an agent working in the workflow reaches it only through that tool; the product ships no gate on its users' history either. The record gate is deleted from the hooks, CI and the runtime.
